newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds edge forward as U.S. dominates trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds edge forward as U.S. dominates trade.

text.p: Irish bonds edged forward in thin late trade on Thursday as the U.S. dominated markets ahead of the release of key economic data on Friday, dealers said.
Dealers said the market awaited the release of U.S. Q4 price index and real GDP data at 1330 GMT while January Chicago PMI and December new home sales figures are expected at 1500 GMT.
"The market is U.S. driven but that hasn't had a major effect here. We have seen reasonable interest in the 10-year area from overseas," one dealer said.
"There was a fair bit of switching out of the five-year into the 10-year yesterday and we saw another bit of that this morning. It has been very much a case of range-trading," the dealer added.

By 1615 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up five pence from Wednesday's close at 102.55 to yield 5.77 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up also up five pence from the close at 109.35 to yield 6.53 percent.
The U.S. bond market had rallied with the long bond up 15/32 to yield 6.87 percent by 1600 GMT on the back of comments from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan.
Greenspan on Thursday called for the creation of an independent commission to determine annual cost-of-living increases for federal benefit programmes and tax brackets.

In prepared testimony to the Senate Finance Committee, Greenspan argued that the Consumer Price Index, which is currently used as the basis for cost-of-living changes, overstates inflation by 0.5 to 1.5 percentage points a year.
Greenspan's prepared testimony dwelt entirely on the CPI bias issue. He did not comment on current economic conditions.
Looking ahead, dealers said market focus was on next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
The general consensus in the market place was that the Fed would not introduce a rate rise next week, dealers said.
